discovery: Electromagnetic metamaterials, negative refraction and transformation optics
motivation: Pendry showed that structured composites of sub-wavelength elements can have engineered permittivity and permeability, including artificial magnetism, and proposed the perfect lens using negative refraction. Smith and co-workers made the first left-handed metamaterial and demonstrated negative refraction experimentally. Pendry, Schurig and Smith, and independently Leonhardt, then introduced transformation optics. In this framework the geometry of space acts as a design tool for controlling electromagnetic fields, and it led to the first demonstrated cloak. Together these ideas turned light–matter interaction into something we can design: refractive index, dispersion and field confinement can now be chosen almost freely. The impact goes well beyond optics. The approach has spread to acoustics, thermal transport and seismology, and it underlies today's metasurfaces, flat lenses, structured-light generators and coherently tunable photonic media. These are now used in laboratories and industry worldwide, including in India.
